rgb: The camera wearer sits looking downward at a tiled floor with a white towel across their lap (3 to 5 metres below the camera) and a low white-and-cyan rectangular platform with a black oval cutout directly in front of them at 3 to 5 metres. Another person sits opposite on a cyan seat roughly 3 to 5 metres away and out of reach, facing away from the camera wearer, though only their lower legs in dark trousers and bare feet with white toe separators are visible near the top of the frame while their upper body and head remain out of view above the upper edge. This second person's feet are spaced about 3 to 5 metres apart on either side of the black cutout, while a rack of upright bottles sits on the floor to the left of the platform (about 3 to 5 metres from the camera wearer and 3 to 5 metres from the platform). In frame 1, the camera wearer holds a plastic-lined blue oval basin in both hands about 3 to 5 metres away directly above the platform, occluding the platform's left side and the other person's right foot, before turning leftward across frames 2 and 3 to place the basin onto the floor to the left of the platform at about 3 to 5 metres distance. Across frames 4 and 5, the camera wearer turns back toward the center-right—bringing a white side table at 3 to 5 metres on the far right holding a blue basket, a yellow bottle, and hand tools into view—and lifts the white towel with both hands to 3 to 5 metres in front of the camera, where the raised cloth partially occludes the platform and the floor basin. Throughout the sequence, the towel, blue basin, platform, the other person's feet, and the right-side tool table all remain far and out of arm's reach (3 to 5 metres) of the camera wearer.
depth: The monocular depth map shows a top-down view where the seated camera wearer looks down at their own arms, hands, and lap (brightest, 3–5 m away) facing away from a second seated person across from them whose lower legs and bare feet with toe separators rest on a raised pedicure footrest box (mid-grey, 3–5 m away) about 3–5 m beyond the wearer's hands, above a dark tiled floor (3–5 m below the camera). Across frames 1 to 3, the camera wearer lifts an oval blue basin from above the footrest (around 3–5 m away, partially occluding the footrest and the other person's left foot in frame 1) and sets it down to the left on the floor (approaching into darker grey at 3–5 m in frames 3–4), before lifting a white towel from their lap farther from the camera (3–5 m) in frames 4–5 while a tall supply cart enters on the far right at 3–5 m. Both the footrest, the basin, the towel, the cart, and the other person's feet remain far and out of arm's reach of the camera wearer, while the other person's upper body and head are completely out of view above the top edge so whether they look away from the wearer cannot be seen directly, though their feet point away from the wearer. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height of the elevated footrest and right-side supply cart from the recessed floor and tracks the basin's downward trajectory from lap height to floor level. However, the depth map is unreliable in frame 3 where the other person's upper-right legs and the footrest box are over-brightened to appear farther than the wearer's hands, and in frame 4 where the black cushion on the footrest is rendered as a smooth convex bulge rather than a flat surface.
segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates distant regions in the pedicure workspace, showing the camera wearer's extended arms at the bottom (3–5 m from the camera), the oval basin in the center-to-left region (moving from 3–5 m down to 3–5 m on the floor across frames 1–3), and the second person's lower legs and feet at the top-right (3–5 m away and out of reach, facing away from the camera wearer with their upper body out of frame). Across frames 1 to 3, the basin mask shifts leftward and grows as it is lowered from above the footrest to the floor on the left, removing the occlusion over the footrest, while in frames 4 and 5 a single large mask covers the wearer's arms, lap towel, and the other person's feet at the center and bottom. The basin, towel, and the other person's feet are all far and out of arm's reach of the camera wearer (3–5 m), spaced 3–5 m apart from one another. While the masks highlight the sharp silhouette and leftward displacement of the oval basin and distant limbs against the unsegmented floor, the map is highly unreliable in both semantics and instance separation. It misclassifies the blue pedicure basin as a 'frisbee' in frames 1–2 and a 'person' in frame 3, splits the camera wearer's right and left arms and the other person's legs into separate 'person' instances in frames 2–3, merges the wearer's arms, white towel, footrest cushion, and the other person's feet into a single 'person' mask in frames 4–5, and completely misses the footrest box, nail polish rack, and right-side tool cart.
pose: The pose map plots 2D body skeletons (yellow) and hand keypoints (magenta) in the camera wearer's distant workspace (3–5 m away), capturing the wearer's right and left hands gripping the rims of the basin in frames 1 and 2 as it moves leftward, only the wearer's left hand on the basin rim in frame 3, and both hands raised farther from the camera (3–5 m) holding the white towel in frames 4 and 5. In frames 4 and 5, it allows tracking the outward divergence of the wearer's hands (from ~3 m apart on the basin to ~5 m apart bunching the towel) and shows the elbows flexing inward on either side of the lap, far and out of arm's reach of the other person's feet just above them (3–5 m away). It makes the fine finger flexion and grip orientation of the wearer's hands explicit even when partially occluded by the basin rim or white towel folds in the RGB image. However, the pose map is severely unreliable for overall scene layout and multi-person understanding because it completely fails to detect the camera wearer's right hand in frame 3 and misses the second person's legs and feet in frames 2–5. Furthermore, because the egocentric top-down viewpoint truncates both people's heads and torsos, the pose estimator hallucinates tiny, inverted full-body torso-and-head skeletons onto the other person's feet and footrest in frame 1 and onto the camera wearer's lap towel and arms in frames 4 and 5, providing false body orientation cues.
